_why: Cross-conversation delivery has two explicit routes: an idle recipient starts a turn, where requested model and effort overrides apply; a running recipient receives session/steer, where overrides cannot apply. Steer ACK means queue admission, not application. The notice makes that distinction visible and directs senders to check queued messages and replies before resending. Stable queue UUIDs and expectedTurnId preserve input identity and fence admission to the intended turn. Stopped/failed recipients keep pending input and require explicit owner resume; timeout remains unconfirmed and late applied can recover. Delegation envelopes carry sender identity to the model while displayText remains owner-facing. Private, deleted, internal and self targets are refused before engine calls; unattended delivery is refused when a human approval would be required. Remote delivery preserves destination and source host IDs, and an unavailable explicit host cannot silently fall through to a local conversation. Remote read routing is pinned in remote-thread-tools-vectors.json. Ultra is a local orchestration choice and must survive delegated turn overrides without folding into Max. Successful send receipts include a nonblocking, host-preserving wait action. Delivery alone does not collect the recipient result, and callers read completed replies after waiting instead of relying on an automatic return message.
